trigger: Breach of security (unauthorized access to electronic personal information) of Florida residents. Here: visitor driver license or ID numbers (SYS-11), employee Social Security numbers and bank data (SYS-12), tenant app user names with passwords (SYS-14), and biometric data (501.171(1)(g)1.a.(VI); face templates from the AI-002 pilot are treated as biometric data, although whether templates computed from camera video qualify under 501.702 is unsettled). Whether badge access history or plate reads count as 'information regarding an individual's geolocation' (item (VII)) is for counsel
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and without unreasonable delay, no later than 30 days after the determination of a breach or reason to believe a breach occurred. Clock starts at the determination, not at discovery; record the date in the decision log
notify: Each affected Florida resident, by mail or email; notice gives the date or date range, the data involved, and a contact (501.171(4)(e)). Substitute notice only in the cases in 501.171(4)(f)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes, if personal information was accessed. BAS ransomware limited to BAS servers (operational data and drawings) usually does not trigger it; the access platform runbook often will

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after the determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred. The 15-day extension in 501.171(3)(a) applies only to the individual notice under (4), if good cause is given to the department in writing within the 30 days; it never extends this department notice
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs, with the content in 501.171(3)(b): synopsis, number of Floridians affected, services offered, copy of the individual notice, and a contact
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more Florida residents (the visitor archive alone holds about 610,000 records until the POAM-017 purge)

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies (as defined in 15 U.S.C. 1681a(p)): timing, distribution, and content of the notices

trigger: After an appropriate investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the company reasonably determines the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Written determination provided to the department within 30 days after the determination; kept for at least 5 years
applies_at_this_tier: Only if counsel supports the determination

trigger: A law enforcement agency determines that individual notice would interfere with a criminal investigation
deadline: Delay for the period in the agency's written request; the agency may extend or revoke it in writing
notify: Hold individual notices; keep the written request

obligation: Third-party agent breach notice to the company (inbound)
trigger: A vendor that maintains, stores, or processes personal information for the company (access control and video platform, visitor management, tenant app, HR and payroll, property management system) has a breach
deadline: The vendor must notify the company no later than 10 days after determining the breach; the company then owes the 501.171(3) and (4) notices. The security addendum asks for 72 hours (POL-01 4.8)
notify: The company (General Counsel and Security Manager)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes. 25 of 41 vendor contracts have no notice term today (POAM-016)

citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Affected individuals (tenant employees, visitors, employees) who reside outside Florida
notify: Residents and regulators per each state's law
applies_at_this_tier: Check the residence of every affected individual; visitors to the towers may live anywhere

citation: 2024 lease template security clause; negotiated 72-hour clauses in 31 leases
trigger: Unauthorized access to tenant employee data held in the access control platform or tenant app
deadline: 31 tenants: within 72 hours as defined in each lease (counsel to confirm when each clock starts; plan from discovery). Other 2024-template leases: promptly. Older leases: no clause, but notify with the others
notify: Each tenant's designated contact, by the lease notice method (Property Managers keep the tenant notice register offline)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes, contractual, not legal. Also send service interruption notices under each lease when building services are degraded

trigger: Significant security incident or building systems outage affecting Tower 3, Tower 4, Retail 5, or Mixed-Use 2, or affecting JV data
notify: JV partner's asset manager (CFO calls, then written notice)

trigger: Events the loan agreements define as reportable (CFO to confirm per loan; typically material adverse events or casualty affecting a property)
applies_at_this_tier: Contractual; CFO checks each agreement during the incident

citation: Merchant agreement; PCI DSS v4.0.1 Req. 12.10.1 (SAQ P2PE) incident response plan
trigger: Suspected compromise of card data or tampering with a P2PE terminal
deadline: Per the merchant agreement and the P2PE Instruction Manual (Controller to confirm the time in the agreement)
applies_at_this_tier: Only if card data or terminals are involved. BAS ransomware and platform incidents do not reach the stand-alone terminals

deadline: Per policy; call the carrier's breach hotline before engaging any vendor so costs are covered

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: All U.S. persons. Strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties

obligation: Voluntary report to CISA and the FBI
trigger: Severity 1 ransomware or other significant cyber incident
notify: CISA (incident reporting on cisa.gov) and the FBI field office or IC3
applies_at_this_tier: Voluntary today; it supports OFAC mitigation and may bring technical help

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident (reasonable belief) or ransom payment by a covered entity
deadline: Statute: 72 hours after reasonable belief of a covered incident; 24 hours after a ransom payment. Not in effect until the final rule is effective
applies_at_this_tier: Not yet: no final rule as of 2026-10-06. The company would be covered under the NPRM's size criterion (it exceeds the SBA size standard), so check the final rule's status at decision point D8 of each incident

obligation: SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05 material cybersecurity incident disclosure
trigger: Registrant determines a cybersecurity incident is material
deadline: Within four business days after determining the incident is material
applies_at_this_tier: No. The company is privately held

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or services discovered
citation: FAR 52.204-25(d) (Section 889); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies covered telecommunications equipment or services (including covered video surveillance equipment) in use or delivered
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification (further report within 10 business days). Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No. The company holds no federal contracts or leases to federal agencies (confirmed by the General Counsel). Recheck before any federal lease, because the camera fleet has not been screened for covered brands

citation: FAR 52.204-23(c); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies a covered article (Kaspersky Lab hardware, software, or services) in use or delivered
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification (further report within 10 business days). Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
